change.summary: GET /data/2.5/onecall and /data/2.5/onecall/timemachine were retired in favour of /data/3.0/onecall. The response schema is nearly identical, so this is not a schema break — it is an entitlement break: the path stays, the key stops being authorised, and the call returns 401 {"cod":401,"message":"Invalid API key..."}. Migration also requires a separate paid subscription with a card on file, not just a URL edit.

spec.note: No OpenAPI anywhere: openweathermap.org/openapi.json and api.openweathermap.org/openapi.json both 404, and apis.guru has no entry. The docs are hand-written HTML, so nothing machine-diffable ever existed.

changelog.note: The most unusual finding in the dataset. For roughly 19 months the deprecation banner WAS on the docs page — wrapped in an HTML comment, so it never rendered. A human reading the page saw nothing; a crawler reading raw HTML would have seen it in August 2022, about 22 months early. Recorded as detected because a crawler genuinely would have caught it, but it is a warning as much as a win: a crawler that reads unrendered markup will also surface things the vendor did not mean to say, and the visible notice did not appear until 2024-03-24.

contract.note: Requires an authorised call, not a liveness check. The path still resolves today — probed 2026-09-19, it returns 401 rather than 404 — so a prober without a real key sees nothing meaningful. Detection here needed a NEW key: from around August 2022 newly issued keys already 401'd while existing keys kept working for another 22 months, which no announcement ever mentioned.

notes: effective_at is a month, not a day: OpenWeather never published one. The docs flipped from 'will be deprecated in June 2024' (2024-06-15 capture) to 'has been deprecated on June 2024' (2024-07-08), and a user reports it stopping around 2024-06-02. 2024-06-01 is therefore the earliest defensible point in the stated window. announced_at uses the first VISIBLE notice rather than the commented-out one, because scoring an invisible announcement as an announcement would flatter the changelog signal. The published date also slipped: 'April 15, 2024' became 'June 2024' roughly two days after the date it had promised, so a monitor keyed on announced dates would have raised a false alarm. A telegraf issue was still open more than a year after retirement.
